content:
The woman hailed as "Mother of the Year" by the San Francisco Giants broadcast team has spoken out to defend her husband after she was widely panned by internet users in a viral video.

The couple and their daughter became an internet sensation after footage from the stairs at Oracle Park last Tuesday showed the woman carrying a baby in one arm and several food containers in the other while her husband appeared oblivious, eating away as his seemingly overburdened wife stood aside.

Commentators Duane Kuiper and Mike Krukow heaped praise on the mother's multitasking abilities, calling her an "Olympic champion" and "Mother of the Year." The pair cast the father in the frame as a villain who just wanted ketchup refills and showed no consideration, and internet users were quick to agree.

So Erika, who did not disclose her surname, decided to hit back.

In an article published on Substack on September 25, she wrote: "Millions of people have watched me carrying my daughter and walking back to my seat with food at a San Francisco Giants game. They called me 'Mother of the Year' and used countless words to insult my husband. Some people messaged me privately, and some made TikTok commentary videos saying I should leave him."

She went on: "My name is Erika. Our baby is called Anastasia. My husband is called Ramses. Before you judge the state of our marriage, please hear what this woman you're rallying behind has to say."

Erika continued to make her case in the article:

"Ramses is a wonderful husband and a great father. We have known each other for nine years and are now raising two children under two together. I know exactly how he treats me, how much he loves our kids, and everything he does for this family. A conversation the audience couldn't hear has become the basis on which millions of people are passing judgment on this life."

She also wrote that Ramses had originally offered to look after Anastasia when she needed to use the restroom (she later decided to go get food instead). He had also asked if she wanted to eat first, and whether she wanted him to carry the containers. She had told him not to bother, because he was feeling low after the death of a close friend.

She wrote: "Our marriage allows either of us to lean on the other when we need to. That night, I chose to look after him. The camera caught one thing I did for my husband, but it can't show all the countless things he has done for me."
